gloss: to grow thickly; to be overgrown; to be lush

definitions.gloss: to grow thickly; to be overgrown; to be lush
definitions.explanation: For plants, trees, or vegetation to grow densely and abundantly.

examples.japanese: {雑草|ざっそう}が{生|お}い{茂|しげ}っている。
{庭|にわ}の{木|き}が{生|お}い{茂|しげ}って{日|ひ}が{入|はい}らなくなった。
examples.english: The trees in the garden grew so thickly that sunlight stopped getting in.

examples.japanese: {熱帯|ねったい}{雨林|うりん}では{巨大|きょだい}な{木々|きぎ}が{生|お}い{茂|しげ}り、{地面|じめん}にはほとんど{光|ひかり}が{届|とど}かない。
examples.english: In the tropical rainforest, enormous trees grow thickly, and almost no light reaches the ground.

notes:
A literary and descriptive verb that paints a vivid picture of dense, luxuriant vegetation. Composed of {生|お}いる (to grow) and {茂|しげ}る (to be thick/lush). It is frequently used in novels, nature descriptions, and travel writing. Often appears in the て-form ({生|お}い{茂|しげ}って) to describe a state.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {草|くさ}が{生|お}い{茂|しげ}る: grass grows thickly
- {木々|きぎ}が{生|お}い{茂|しげ}る: trees grow lush
- {雑草|ざっそう}が{生|お}い{茂|しげ}る: weeds become overgrown
- {緑|みどり}が{生|お}い{茂|しげ}る: greenery flourishes

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {茂|しげ}る: to grow thick; to be dense — the simpler form, also used for vegetation but less emphatic
- {繁茂|はんも}する: to grow densely — a more scientific or formal synonym
- {生|は}える: to grow; to sprout — focuses on new growth emerging, not density
